metadata.title: Secure Resilience Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for ensuring systems can survive, degrade, halt, or recover without introducing new harm or unsafe conditions.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Resilience, continuity, recovery, degradation, isolation, and safe-halt mechanisms across IT, integration, and cyber-physical domains.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining resilience eligibility, reversibility boundaries, and permitted recovery outcomes.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines resilience state, reversibility, and resume eligibility as trust-relevant signal data.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Continuity Planning controls (CP-2 through CP-10) are interpreted through Secure-Resilience eligibility constraints.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance asserting that recovery and resumption must be explicitly authorized and context-aware.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Provides guidance on coordinating resilience decisions and recovery activities across stakeholders. Does not define recovery eligibility or safety.

metadata.remarks: Secure Resilience Core defines when recovery, restoration, continuation, or halt actions are permissible. This pattern does not perform backup, recovery, failover, or continuity operations. It establishes non-equivalence between resilience mechanisms and safe outcomes.

components.title: State Reversibility Classification
components.description: Classification of system and process state as reversible, partially reversible, or irreversible.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Resilience planning considers reversibility of system state.

components.title: Recovery Eligibility Determination
components.description: Determines whether restoration or reconstitution is safe to perform given current state.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Recovery actions are conditioned on eligibility and safety context.

components.title: Permitted Resilience Outcomes
components.description: Defines allowable outcomes such as restore, degrade, halt, isolate, or decommission.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Alternate processing outcomes are defined and bounded.

components.title: Resume Eligibility
components.description: Determines when a system may safely return to operational service.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Resumption of operations is explicitly governed.

components.title: Resilience Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what resilience mechanisms do not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Backup, recovery, or continuity does not imply safety, correctness, or authorization to resume.
